P1.evidence: Setter handoff was referenced but not read back — 'I know you spoke with Kyla... So I kind of have an understanding of where you're at' — which names the setter without reflecting any of her notes, so the prospect is told rather than shown he was seen. The frame was two-part again: 'go a little bit deeper where you're at right now, what it is that you want. If I feel like we can help, great' — no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement was taken ('Alrighty? Okay.' / 'Cool. Yes.') and the open question ran clean: 'What were you hoping we can help you with?'

P2.evidence: The pain intake was genuinely excellent and the best thing in the call — 'Talk to me about the hip, what's going on there?', then quality ('Is it like a sharp pain, a dull pain, a nagging pain?'), then location, then radiation, then a specific sciatica differential, then the same sequence again for the back. Everything else was skipped. Age was volunteered ('I'm nearly 50'); height and weight never asked. Occupation never asked at all — which is why the six-month unpaid sabbatical starting in three days did not surface until 00:29:28, after the price. Diet never asked (he volunteered he was happy with it), sleep never asked, and energy never asked despite the man being burnt out. Training was covered only to the level of 'a combination of weights, cardio, cycling, swimming' with no frequency or days.

P3.evidence: The phase never left the surface. 'If you were to fast forward six months down the line, like, where would you want to be?' produced the mobility and flexibility answer, which is P3b, and that was the ceiling. The bridge was attempted — 'what's had you wanting to get some help again?' — and the prospect deflected: 'I don't actually know. I'm just curious what you have on offer.' The rep accepted that and moved to pitching how the coaching works rather than re-approaching. Nothing about who else it impacts, nothing about family, identity or legacy, and no meaningful reflect-back beyond the literal restatement 'So the mobility and not having pain is really what you want.' The prospect's genuine driver — burnout severe enough to stop working for six months — was never reached, and he handed it over unprompted twenty minutes later.

P4.evidence: Effectively skipped. The only past-attempts material is the prospect volunteering 'I used to have a PT for years so I stopped having my PT when I moved to the UK that was 10 years ago', which the rep echoed back inside another question rather than opened up. No 'what happened with that', no 'why didn't it stick', no root cause, no naming of the gap, and no version of 'the information isn't the problem'. With ten years of self-directed training and a failed surgical route, this was the richest available seam in the call and it was left untouched.

P5.evidence: Not run in any form. No two-year picture, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The closest thing to a consequence frame was the rep's own aside at 00:13:36 — 'there's two types of people in your scenario, a person who keeps pushing forward, then there's a person who just gives up' — which the prospect had already answered for himself and which asked nothing of him. There was no cost of inaction on the table when the number landed.

P6.evidence: P6a ran and ran early: 'Do you feel like we can help you kind of get to where you want to be, put you in the best place?' The answer was 'I think so, yes' — hedged, and the rep took it. P6b was never asked, so nothing was isolated before the price. P6c is a clear fail: the script says move forward only on a clear YES and return to Phase 5 on hesitation, and the rep moved from a hedged 'I think so' straight into next steps, guarantee and price.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted but the prospect deferred to the following day, so payment, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement email and the welcome-email/Skool walkthrough were all unreachable. The Trevor call was pre-framed for the Monday ('Book you in this call with Trevor, which would likely be on Monday') but never booked.

objection_plays.detail: 'I will sleep on it, and I will get back to you tomorrow' is the trigger in substance, and none of the seven scripted moves ran. No 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal' at the point of the deferral, no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no decision-pattern challenge. The rep went straight to scheduling the follow-up and then spent two and a half minutes on the mechanics of a 13:30 slot.

The one good move was the isolation question at 00:29:14 — 'Is it a case of, like, I want to do it, how do I make it work? Or is it like a should I do it kind of thing?' — which correctly established this was a money problem and not a belief problem ('it's not about if I should... I know I should. I want to'). Everything after that stopped. Zero of the six FINANCIAL PICTURE moves ran: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no used-versus-available, no investments. 'Most people just take care of it upfront' was used as an anchor rather than as the bridge into 'for some we break it up — want to explore making it work?', and when the split was eventually offered it was improvised with visible arithmetic trouble.

The sabbatical starting on 1 June is a textbook OD trigger in substance — a life event three days out that makes now feel like the wrong moment financially. The rep not only failed to run the play, he reinforced the objection: 'That's beautiful. I'm happy for you. That would be a nice, a nice little break, huh?' None of the moves ran — no 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'what if all you had to do was show up'. The stronger available angle, that six months off work is the ideal window to rebuild a hip and a back, was visible and unused; the manager identified exactly this in the same-day 1-1: 'But that's more reason for him to do the program.'

Clinical fit. The prospect has MRI-confirmed hip impingement, a failed arthroscopy, constant pain, a surgeon deferring replacement, and secondary back pain — and the script has no path for establishing whether loaded ballistic kettlebell work is appropriate, or for obtaining clinician clearance before selling. This is the known gap the playbook already records from the Tyron Giuliani call, recurring here with a prospect who was moving toward purchase. The rep's only handling was reassurance that 'everything we do is tailored... especially considering the hip and the back', which is a sales answer to a clinical question.

notes: The medical intake was excellent and the rest of discovery barely happened — P4 and P5 were not run at all and P3 stalled at the surface, so the rep reached the price with no why, no cost of inaction and no idea what the man does for a living. That last gap is the concrete lesson: had P2b been asked, the sabbatical would have surfaced at minute five instead of minute twenty-nine and the entire call could have been built around it. The rep's own read in the 1-1 hours later was correct — 'I should have open walleted him, but I didn't' — but the failure started much earlier than the objection handle. Coach on: ask what they do for work, run P4 and P5 before pitching, and stop computing payment splits out loud.
